What does Next.js find for `/posts`?
app⌁ page.tsx⌄ posts⌁ page.tsx
Terminal
$ GET /
Matched app/page.tsx
✓ Home page generated
example.com/
Welcome backOpen the post list from the URL above
How a URL becomes a prepared page

The URL maps to a file: In the App Router, /posts maps to app/posts/page.tsx.

The server prepares content for the browser: The page can fetch an article list and prepare HTML on the server before sending it to the browser, reducing white-screen wait times.

Mark interactive components with 'use client': Components run on the server by default. Those requiring user interaction (onClick, useState) must have 'use client' at the top. The common 'useState only works in Client Components' error means this directive is missing.

What people often confuse

One Next.js project can contain server and browser code, and you must explicitly mark browser code with 'use client'. Secrets must stay on the server side and never be sent to the browser.

**The server prepares content for the browser:**The page can fetch an article list and prepare HTML on the server before sending it to the browser, reducing white-screen wait times.

**Mark interactive components with 'use client':**Components run on the server by default. Those requiring user interaction (onClick, useState) must have 'use client' at the top. The common 'useState only works in Client Components' error means this directive is missing.
**What people often confuse**
One Next.js project can contain server and browser code, and you must explicitly mark browser code with 'use client'. Secrets must stay on the server side and never be sent to the browser.
